coverage_of_risk.rationale: The app contains no tests at all, so none of the genuinely risky logic (data assembly, dedup/form exclusion, sorting, URL state) is covered by anything the app owns; only the provided acceptance suite exercises any of it.

behaviour_not_implementation.rationale: No tests exist, so there is nothing to classify; the criterion scores at the floor.

evidence: app/src/lib/format.js:1-6 — humanize regression would alter headings on every page, undetected by app tests
app/src/lib/server/pokeapi.js:31-34 — idFromUrl regex change would break every species mapping silently
app/src/routes/+page.svelte:10-17 — unvalidated initial ?type= vs validated syncFromUrl at +page.svelte:76-86, a latent inconsistency no test would catch
regression_power.rationale: Nothing the app authored can fail; any refactor of the data layer, sorting comparator, or URL-state handling would ship broken with only the page-level acceptance suite (which pins a narrow set of URLs and values) as a backstop.

evidence: app/src — no test files at all, hence no padding or duplication
signal_to_noise.rationale: Per the rubric, no tests scores 3: there is no noise, but also no signal.

findings.issue: No test script, no test runner, and zero test files anywhere in app/; every behavior is guarded only by the harness-owned acceptance suite, which is not part of the repo the team will own.
findings.suggestion: Add Vitest (plus @testing-library/svelte for components) with a 'test' script, and at minimum unit-test the pure data functions in src/lib and src/lib/server/pokeapi.js against small API fixtures.

findings.issue: cardsFromPokemonRefs encapsulates the highest-risk invariants — id>=10000 alternate-form exclusion, seen-dedup, dex-number ordering, and the hidden-ability extra merge — with no test; a refactor could re-introduce Mega forms or duplicate cards on three different pages at once.
findings.suggestion: Unit test it with synthetic refs including forms above 10000, duplicates, and out-of-order IDs, asserting the card list that results.

findings.issue: The sort comparator (missing-last in both directions, numeric vs localeCompare, moveLabel tiebreaker, single-column aria-sort) is subtle and only partially pinned by the acceptance suite (Power column, one table); flipping the missing-value branch when descending is an easy regression.
findings.suggestion: Add component or extracted-function tests covering ascending, descending, missing-values, and tie-breaking for both level-up and non-level tables.

findings.issue: Initial URL filter state is read without validation (bogus ?type= or ?generation= silently yields 'No Pokémon found') while syncFromUrl (+page.svelte:76-86) validates against data; the inconsistency is untested and behaves differently on hard load vs back-navigation.
findings.suggestion: Route initial state through the same validation as syncFromUrl, and add a test loading /?type=bogus expecting the 'All types' view.

findings.issue: memo cache semantics (rejected promises evicted, 404-nulls cached for the process lifetime) are untested; a refactor that caches failures would pin a transient API error for every user of the node process.
findings.suggestion: Unit test memo with a failing then succeeding fetch, and with a 404, asserting eviction and caching behavior explicitly.

findings.issue: Method-table ordering (METHOD_ORDER rank, then alphabetical for others) and default-game selection (games.at(-1)) are untested; a reordered rank array or switched comparison would shuffle sections with no failing test.
findings.suggestion: Load-function test with a small moves payload asserting table order, level-up default sort, and selected-game default.

findings.issue: The RELATIONS key→label mapping is positional data wiring with no test; swapping two keys (e.g. half_damage_to/no_damage_to) would render correct-looking labels over wrong relations.
findings.suggestion: Assert the relations list order and key mapping for a known type fixture.

findings.issue: humanize underpins every heading and list label; edge inputs (null, empty segments, already-capitalized, multi-dash like 'flabebe-red-striped') are untested.
findings.suggestion: A table-driven unit test of humanize costs almost nothing and pins the display-name rule.

summary: The app ships zero tests of its own — no runner, no script, no spec files — leaving the acceptance suite as the only guard, and that suite is owned by the harness, not the codebase. The untested surface is exactly where regressions hurt: pure data transforms (humanize, idFromUrl), the alternate-form exclusion/dedup in cardsFromPokemonRefs, the client-side sort comparator, and URL filter-state handling (which already has an unvalidated-initial-state inconsistency at +page.svelte:10-17). Any future data-layer refactor would ship with no failing signal until users noticed wrong cards, ordering, or filters.
